Marta: heads-up — onboarding zebra customer's adapter (LoRA) into int4 runtime. Quick smoke run shows tokenization mismatch on a handful of examples, and BLEU/EM drop for structured responses. Anyone seen this pattern?
Samir: seen similar when tokenizer vocab indices shift after merge. did you use the customer's tokenizer artifact or our canonical one?
Marta: using customer's tokenizer mounted from their bundle. command I used: `python run_smoke.py --model zebra-lora --quant int4 --tokenizer ./zebra_tokenizer/` — output attached in thread (summary below)
Li: can you paste the sample where tokens diverge? quick check: `print(tokenizer.encode(sample))` vs `tokenizer_fast` maybe mismatch between slow/fast
Marta: sample snippet: "Invoice #42 — total due $1,234.56". Our encode -> [101, 25, ... , 9999], zebra_tokenizer -> [101, 25, ... , 10223]. Model output truncates after dollar sign sometimes.
Jake: throwing hypothesis: merge process changed special token mapping (e.g., `#` mapped different ID). Also double-check normalization (NFKC) differences. Quick diff command I run: `python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; ..."` — got different byte offsets.
Samir: infra-bot, can you confirm which tokenizer artifact hash is deployed on the int4 runtime? infra-bot: ci/deploy: tokenizer artifact zebra-tokenizer@sha256:3a7f... deployed to canary-gpu-4 on 2026-02-18T14:03Z
Li: ok hash matches customer's bundle, so merge step likely altered ID map rather than wrong artifact. Repro steps: 1) run encode on host A (python3.10) 2) run encode in runtime container (torch+tokenizers binary). Are they the same?
Marta: repro on runtime container shows the divergent ids too. Samir: can you try converting tokenizer to the HF `PreTrainedTokenizerFast` wrapper — sometimes fast vs slow produce different offsets on punctuation.
Samir: ran quick patch — wrapped with `PreTrainedTokenizerFast(tokenizer_object)` and re-ran smoke. BLEU went from 0.72 -> 0.91 on our small pack for structured responses. Token ids normalized.
Marta: nice. any concerns about doing that automatically for zebra bundle? customer's code expects the original slow tokenizer behaviour — risk of subtle differences.
Li: propose a compatibility shim: keep original tokenizer artifact but ship a small mapping table that remaps problematic special token ids at load time (non-destructive). That keeps semantics while fixing runtime.
Jake: +1. Also add a regression test in the quick-eval pack: a tiny table of tokens -> expected ids for 10 edge examples.
Samir: I can add the mapping generator script. Command: `python tools/generate_tokmap.py --src ./zebra_tokenizer --dst mapping.json` — returns mapping for altered special tokens.
Marta: plan: Samir to add mapping + updated smoke pack; Jake to add regression cases; Li to validate semantics with customer on a short call; I'll schedule canary rollout after tests pass. ETA by EOD Wednesday.
infra-bot: ci/pipeline: smoke-pack test started (zebra-onboard branch) — logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/12345
Marta: thanks all — ping me if you hit blockers. :thumbsup:
